name: Cosmos Institute Grants (AI for Truth-Seeking & Human Autonomy)
amount: Up to USD 10,000 per grant (typically USD 1k-10k; larger considered for exceptional proposals); USD 1M pool of cash + Prime Intellect compute credits
eligibility: Builders/researchers prototyping AI that strengthens human autonomy and truth-seeking; no credentials required
eligibility_note: No formal nationality restriction published; program states anyone can apply.
how_to_apply_tip: Fill the 'Express interest in future rounds' form now; proposals should be a concrete working prototype buildable in 90 days.
deadline_quote: Application window: Latest round closed on Sunday July 26th, 2026.
verdict_reason: Latest round is closed and no next date is given. The official pages publish no eligibility rules, so nationality, institution and individual eligibility are neither confirmed nor excluded.
eligibility_quote: Selected builders receive up to $10,000 and 90 days to build a working prototype, plus a place in a community at the frontier of AI and philosophy. (FAQ: "We primarily support founders and researchers who are working at the frontier of AI")
ask_funder: Can an individual researcher based in Pakistan (Associate Professor at a private college) apply for and receive Cosmos Grants, and when does the next round open?

name: Multi-Agent AI Safety Funding Call (Cooperative AI Foundation, Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind, ARIA)
amount: Tier 1 up to USD 300,000; Tier 2 USD 300,000-1,000,000
eligibility: Universities, research institutes, non-profits; independent researchers need a fiscal sponsor if selected
eligibility_note: Call page: 'Open globally'; non-US institutions can receive funds directly if 501(c)(3)-equivalent (verified via NGOSource).
how_to_apply_tip: Pakistani public universities usually need NGOSource equivalency determination; start that paperwork with your ORIC office well before the next round.
deadline_quote: Applications are due by on August 8th, 2026 by 11:59pm AoE, and we expect to notify applicants of our final decisions in Autumn 2026.
verdict_reason: Teams worldwide may apply, but a non-US lead institution must hold 501(c)(3)-equivalent charitable status. Whether BIC, a private TNE college, qualifies (or whether a fiscal sponsor would be needed) is not confirmed. The 2026 call is closed and no next round has been announced.
eligibility_quote: [Teams from] anywhere in the world are eligible to apply. Non-U.S. universities, research institutes, and nonprofits may serve as the lead applicant and receive funding directly, provided the institution holds a 501(c)(3) designation or an equivalent charitable status. ... Independent researchers may submit proposals. However, if chosen for funding, they must secure a fiscal sponsor or affiliate with an eligible non-profit to manage the award.
ask_funder: Will there be a 2027 round? Can a PI at a private (possibly for-profit) transnational college in Pakistan lead a proposal, or must the award go through a fiscal sponsor or NGOSource-verified nonprofit?

name: Sindh Research Support Programme (SRSP)
amount: Up to PKR 5 million per project (per 2025-26 advertisement; 2026-27 amount not stated on page)
eligibility: Full-time regular PhD faculty (BPS/TTS) at universities in Sindh; one proposal as PI; not funded in previous 2 years; IT & Computer Science is a thematic area
eligibility_note: Only for faculty at Sindh universities (provincial scheme)
how_to_apply_tip: Frame the AI project around a Sindh issue (water, health, climate, education) – provincial-priority and collaborative proposals are preferred.
deadline_quote: CALL FOR RESEARCH PROPOSALS (ADVERTISEMENT – ENGLISH) – SINDH RESEARCH SUPPORT PROGRAMME (2026-27) – Deadline: 23-Oct-2026
verdict_reason: SRSP is limited to regular PhD faculty of public-sector universities or degree-awarding institutes in Sindh. BIC is a private TNE college and not a degree-awarding institute. The 2026-27 call also closed on 2026-10-23.
eligibility_quote: Full time regular PhD or FCPS/MCPS/FRCS faculty member (BPS/TTS) in a Public Sector University/ Degree Awarding Institute. (2025-26 advertisement, 'FOR PUBLIC SECTOR UNIVERSITIES AND DEGREE AWARDING INSTITUTES OF SINDH PROVINCE'); 2026-27 form undertaking: 'That, I am a regular faculty member at ____ and possess PhD / FRCS / FCPS degree from HEC recognized University.'

name: National Research Program for Universities (NRPU)
amount: See website (project budgets set per call)
eligibility: PI must be a regular faculty member/eligible academic at a recognized Pakistani HEI; basic and applied research in all fields incl. CS; junior staff encouraged on teams
eligibility_note: National HEC programme for faculty of Pakistani HEIs; 2026-27 call removed the application fee and the delayed-cases bar; joint proposals with foreign (esp. KSA) researchers encouraged
how_to_apply_tip: Next call likely autumn 2027: draft a project outline now, line up a co-PI/industry partner, and route it through your university ORIC on research.hec.gov.pk.
deadline_quote: New Call for Research Proposals 2026–27 is Live Now – Deadline for Submission is Oct 30, 2026. (FAQ Q11: 'The deadline is Monday, October 30, 2026.')
verdict_reason: The PI must be faculty at a public or private higher education institution in Pakistan that is recognized and meets HEC requirements. It is not confirmed that BIC, a TNE college delivering UK degrees and not HEC-chartered, counts. The 2026-27 call closed on 2026-10-30.
eligibility_quote: Principal Investigator (PI) must: Be a faculty member (PhD or FCPS/MCPS/FRCS) working on regular/ contract basis ... in the Higher Education Institutions (public or private) of Pakistan. FAQ Q19: 'The Principal Investigator (PI) must be a regular faculty member, researcher, or eligible academic staff member affiliated with a recognized Pakistani higher education institution that meets HEC eligibility requirements.'
ask_funder: Is faculty at Beaconhouse International College (a private TNE college delivering University of Essex / LJMU degrees, not HEC-chartered) eligible to be NRPU PI, and can BIC's ORIC register on research.hec.gov.pk? If not, can such faculty be Co-PI?

name: Foresight Institute AI for Science & Safety Grants (Nodes RFP)
amount: Typically USD 30,000-100,000 (larger possible); overhead up to 10%
eligibility: Individuals, teams, non-profits and for-profits; AI safety, local compute, coordination/accountability, AI-first science; outputs must be open-sourced
eligibility_note: RFP page lists no nationality/citizenship restriction; priority to applicants who will be in-person in SF or Berlin hubs; due diligence required.
how_to_apply_tip: Current round closes 31 Oct 2026 (23:59 PDT); if missed, watch foresight.org/grants for the next RFP. Remote applicants should explain how they will engage with the hubs.
deadline_quote: The application deadline for this RFP is 31st October 2026 23:59 PDT.
verdict_reason: Individuals, teams and organizations may apply, and the page sets no nationality, institution, age or career-stage restriction. The deadline is today (2026-10-31, 23:59 PDT), so only hours remain. In-person hub presence is prioritised but not required.
eligibility_quote: Who can apply? We accept applications from individuals, teams, and organizations. Both non-profit and for-profit organizations are welcome to apply, but for-profits should be prepared to motivate why they need grant funding. ... Successful applicants must pass our due diligence process.

name: NLnet Foundation Open Calls (NGI Zero / Restack / CodeSupply funds)
eligibility: Individuals or organisations doing open-source technical development (open licences required)
eligibility_note: Any country can apply, but EU-funded calls usually expect Horizon Europe-eligible applicants; others must justify a 'European dimension'.
how_to_apply_tip: Bimonthly deadlines; partner with a European collaborator or show EU user benefit. Proposal must be human-written (AI use disclosed).
verdict_reason: Pakistan is on NLnet's list of Horizon Europe-eligible countries, so the European-dimension requirement is met. Its applicants participate on the same terms as EU applicants. Grants are for open-source technical development rather than pure research.
eligibility_quote: Our EU-supported funds require a strong European dimension; usually this means applicants should (mostly) be from Horizon Europe-eligible countries. / People and organisations of these eligible countries can participate on the same terms as those from EU member states. (European-dimension page country list includes 'Pakistan')

name: Lacuna Fund RFP: Use Lacuna Fund's open datasets (SDG dataset utilization)
funder: Lacuna Fund (secretariat: ACTS AI Institute; multi-donor)
amount: Up to USD 10,000 per award (three awards; USD 30,000 total)
eligibility: Global South teams (non-profits, research institutions/universities, social enterprises) to train, scale and apply ML models using Lacuna Fund datasets
eligibility_note: Apply page: 'Funding is available for Global South teams'; Fund focuses on 'low- and middle-income contexts globally'. No country list published on page.
how_to_apply_tip: Deadline is in 2 weeks: apply through your university (institutional applicant), name a specific Lacuna dataset (e.g. language/health/agri) you will build models on, and stress SDG impact in Pakistan/South Asia.
verdict_reason: Pakistan qualifies as an LMIC on the Wellcome list. However, the lead must be a non-profit, a research institution or a for-profit social enterprise, and individuals must apply through an institutional sponsor. It is unclear whether BIC, a private TNE college, qualifies as a lead.
eligibility_quote: Be either a non-profit entity, research institution, for-profit social enterprise, or a team of such organisations. Individuals must apply through an institutional sponsor. ... Be headquartered in a low- or middle-income country (LMIC) in the Global South. For a list of eligible countries, refer to the Wellcome Trust LMIC guidance
ask_funder: Does a private transnational higher-education college in Pakistan (Beaconhouse International College) qualify as a 'research institution' lead applicant, or must the PI apply via a non-profit/university institutional sponsor?

name: Career Development and Transition Funding
eligibility: People at any career stage transitioning into work on global catastrophic risks incl. AI safety (independent study, upskilling, transition periods)
eligibility_note: Official page returned 403 to automated fetch; secondary sources describe rolling, worldwide eligibility. Verify on official page.
how_to_apply_tip: Explain clearly how the funded period moves you into an AI safety research career; also check Coefficient Giving's technical AI safety RFP page for open calls.
deadline_quote: Official page could not be opened (HTTP 403 to WebFetch and curl; archive not reachable). Rolling status is not verified.
verdict_reason: The official page could not be opened, so the deadline, nationality and eligibility rules could not be verified against official text.
ask_funder: Is the Career Development and Transition Funding programme still accepting applications on a rolling basis, and can a Pakistan-based Associate Professor (PhD 2025) moving into AI safety research apply?

name: Emergent Ventures
eligibility: Anyone 13+ worldwide with high-impact 'zero to one' ideas; no credentials required
eligibility_note: Supports 'thinkers and doers worldwide'; no country restriction stated (dedicated tranches for India, Africa, etc.).
how_to_apply_tip: Short, punchy application; AI-written applications are explicitly not accepted. Pitch an ambitious AI project with societal impact.
deadline_quote: There is no application deadline for EV AI, but applicants are encouraged to apply quickly, as funds are limited. (Main EV page shows an 'Apply Now' form and no deadline.)
verdict_reason: The programme supports people worldwide and its only stated condition is a minimum age of 13. Nothing excludes a Pakistani academic. AI-written applications are rejected.
eligibility_quote: supporting thinkers and doers worldwide who pursue highly scalable, "zero to one" ideas to meaningfully improve society ... Applicants must be at least 13 years old.

name: Internet Freedom Fund (incl. applied research)
eligibility: Individuals 18+ and organisations; technology or applied research projects helping people facing censorship/surveillance
eligibility_note: Open 'regardless of nationality'; only OFAC-sanctioned countries excluded (Pakistan is not).
how_to_apply_tip: Submit a concept note first (response in ~6-8 weeks); ML-based censorship measurement or deepfake/surveillance detection fits.
deadline_quote: Applications to the Fund go through a two-stage application process and are accepted on a rolling basis.
verdict_reason: Individuals aged 18 or over may apply regardless of nationality, and only US-sanctioned countries are excluded. Pakistan is not under OFAC country-wide sanctions. The project must fit internet freedom (censorship or surveillance).
eligibility_quote: Individuals ages 18+ or organizations (for-profit or nonprofit) irrespective of nationality, creed, or sex are eligible to apply. OTF is not able to support applicants within countries that the United States has trade restrictions or export sanctions as determined by the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

name: PSF Research Support Programme (Mathematics & Computer Sciences)
eligibility: Individual scientists or research groups at Pakistani universities and R&D organizations; ten fields incl. Mathematics & Computer Sciences; concept paper then full proposal
eligibility_note: Domestic programme (964 projects funded); no current call date published – check RGMS notifications
how_to_apply_tip: Register on rgms.psf.gov.pk and submit a concept paper first; also watch PSF bilateral calls (SCO, NSFC-China, TUBITAK, Sri Lanka NSF) announced on the same portal.
deadline_quote: No deadline or rolling statement on the official page; it says only: 'Both the concept paper and the full-length proposal must be submitted via RGMS.'
verdict_reason: The RSP page says only that it funds 'universities and R&D organizations' and gives no PI criteria. PSF's related Competitive Research Programme requires the PI to be from an HEC-recognized university, which BIC is not.
eligibility_quote: the Research Support Programme plays a vital role by providing financial assistance to universities and R&D organizations. (Related PSF CRP page: 'Principal Investigator should be from HEC recognized University or public sector R&D organization')
ask_funder: Can faculty of a private transnational college (Beaconhouse International College, not HEC-chartered) be PI under the PSF Research Support Programme, and is there a current concept-paper window or deadline on RGMS?

name: SFF Funding Rolling Application / S-Process Grant Rounds
amount: Total USD 20-40M+ per year across rounds (per-grant varies)
eligibility: Charities or projects with a fiscal sponsor; individuals need a fiscal sponsor; AI safety among focus areas
eligibility_note: Nonprofits outside US-defined adversarial nations can generally apply; individuals cannot apply without a fiscal sponsor.
how_to_apply_tip: Secure a fiscal sponsor (e.g. a US/UK AI-safety nonprofit) first; rolling application also triggers a Speculation Grant request.
deadline_quote: Applications to S-Process Grant Rounds are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the year, regardless of whether a Grant Round is open or not.
verdict_reason: Charities in any non-adversarial country can be funded, but individuals cannot without a fiscal sponsor that has charity status. BIC's charity status is unknown, so eligibility depends on securing a fiscal sponsor. The 2027 round dates have not been announced.
eligibility_quote: Organizations seeking funding using this form must already have charity status, or be hosted or fiscally sponsored by an organization with charity status. ... SFF cannot recommend funding to individuals/independent researchers who do not have a fiscal sponsor. ... We can recommend funding to charities/non-profits in any country except nations considered adversarial to the US.
ask_funder: Would a project led by a Pakistan-based academic be eligible if fiscally sponsored by a Pakistani or international charity, and when will the 2027 S-Process round deadlines be published?

name: Start-up Research Grant Program (SRGP) for fresh PhDs
eligibility: Fresh PhD (within 2 years) joining as an IPFP Fellow at a public university or a private university eligible for public funding; one-time only
eligibility_note: Pakistani faculty only; current HEC/NAHE page frames SRGP for IPFP (Interim Placement of Fresh PhDs) fellows – confirm whether non-IPFP regular faculty can still apply
how_to_apply_tip: You get only one chance and incomplete files are rejected: collect 3 vendor quotations, signed ORIC/VC undertaking and budget sheet before submitting the online form.
deadline_quote: A faculty member on IPFP needs to apply for Start-up Research Grant within 01 months of his/her joining.
verdict_reason: SRGP is only for fresh PhDs who join a public university, or a private one eligible for public funding, as IPFP Fellows. You are an experienced Associate Professor at a private TNE college, not an IPFP fellow. Your PhD, awarded in January 2024, is also past the 2-year 'fresh PhD' window.
eligibility_quote: Fresh Ph.D. degree holder who has recently joined a public sector or private sector university eligible for public funding (first time after Ph.D.) as IPFP Fellow on Interim Placement of Fresh Ph.D. (IPFP). / Experienced faculty members/researcher or Faculty of Private Institutions are not eligible for Government funding

name: Transformative AI Fund (successor to Long-Term Future Fund)
eligibility: Individuals, new and existing organisations; technical AI safety research, policy, forecasting, field-building, training
eligibility_note: Official page states no country restriction and funds individuals; Long-Term Future Fund is closed and replaced by this fund.
how_to_apply_tip: Short online form (<1h). Frame a concrete 6-12 month AI safety project (e.g. interpretability/evals) with a modest budget; small, well-scoped asks from early-career researchers are common.
deadline_quote: We are always open to applications.
verdict_reason: The fund grants to individuals and states no geographic, age or institutional restriction. An AI safety or AI-risk project from a Pakistan-based researcher is within remit.
eligibility_quote: We make early-stage grants to individuals, new organizations, and existing organizations with new projects, addressing transformative AI, with a primary focus on reducing global catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems.

name: COMSTECH-IFS Research Grants Programme
eligibility: Early-career scientists in OIC member states; historically agriculture/environment/food sciences
eligibility_note: Pakistan listed among funded countries (49 grantees, USD 559,834 cumulative 1998-2023).
how_to_apply_tip: Fits AI applied to agriculture/water/food (e.g. image-based crop disease detection, as in a 2023 Pakistani award). Note: ifs.se domain no longer belongs to IFS; confirm the current IFS call channel via COMSTECH.
deadline_quote: No call, deadline or eligibility text on the official COMSTECH programme pages, which show only past allocations and grantee counts up to 2023.
verdict_reason: The official pages give no current call, eligibility rules or IFS call channel. IFS has historically used early-career limits that a 36-45-year-old may or may not meet, but these are not stated on the official pages.
eligibility_quote: The essential purpose of the collaboration is to enhance research capability within the OIC region, and to reap a rich harvest by obtaining matching grants from IFS (US$ 0.1 million/year) for OIC scientists and institutions.
ask_funder: Is the COMSTECH-IFS programme still active for 2026-27? If so, what are the eligibility limits (age, years since PhD, fields, institution type)? My PhD was awarded in January 2024. Does AI/robotics applied to agriculture or water qualify?
